name: Degree-20 real spherical harmonic L4 concentration on S2
definition: Among nonzero real homogeneous harmonic polynomials of degree 20 in three variables, maximize the normalized L4/L2 ratio on the unit sphere S2: J=(M4/M2^2)^(1/4), where Mp is the uniform probability-surface average of |P|^p.
solution_format: An object with coefficients: a list of 231 rational numbers in the documented monomial order x^a y^b z^(20-a-b). Each coefficient is an integer or an exact rational string. No coefficient-size bound is imposed.
constraints: The input polynomial is homogeneous of degree exactly 20 in x,y,z.
The polynomial is real, nonzero, and its ordinary Euclidean Laplacian is identically zero.

The domain uses rational coefficients. Rational harmonic polynomials are dense in the real 41-dimensional harmonic subspace, so they have the same supremum for this continuous scale-invariant objective.
The objective uses uniform probability measure on S2; M2=average |P|^2 and M4=average |P|^4.
No coefficient magnitude or denominator cap is imposed.
verification: The checker proves homogeneity by fixed degree-20 monomial indexing, computes the exact rational Laplacian, and exactly integrates P^2 and P^4 using monomial moments on S2. It returns the exact fourth-root expression and a conservative rational lower bound with an enclosing interval.
